title: Best IB Chemistry Exam Calculator and Tools
summary: Choose an allowed IB Chemistry exam calculator, understand current IB rules, and learn efficient calculator and data booklet techniques for every paper.
body_markdown:
An **IB Chemistry exam calculator is required for Paper 1A, Paper 1B, and Paper 2** under the syllabus first assessed in 2025. For most students, the best option is a familiar approved scientific calculator or the graphing calculator already used in IB Mathematics.


Permission depends on the exact model, operating system, stored content, and examination settings. Your IB coordinator must verify the current guidance before the examination, even if your model appears on an older approved list.


### What calculators are allowed in IB Chemistry?


The[official IB exam calculator policy](https://ibo.org/programmes/diploma-programme/assessment-and-exams/exam-calculator-policy/) explains that not every calculator, application, or program is suitable for examinations. Detailed model-level instructions are supplied to schools through the IB Programme Resource Centre.


Recent publicly indexed guidance includes these examples, although permitted models and required settings can change:


Calculator family Recent examples Important condition


Texas Instruments TI-83 Plus and TI-84 Plus models Memory and unauthorized applications must be cleared as instructed


TI-Nspire CX and CX II non-CAS models The required operating system and Press-to-Test settings must be used


Selected TI-Nspire CAS Certain CX II CAS models CAS must be disabled using the prescribed configuration


Casio graphing calculators fx-9750GIII, fx-9860GIII, fx-CG50, and specified equivalents Approved software and **Examination Mode for IB** may be required


HP Prime and NumWorks Supported current models Correct firmware and IB exam mode are required


Scientific calculators Compliant non-programmable models Powers, roots, logarithms, exponentials, and scientific notation are recommended


This table does not guarantee permission for an individual device. Ask your coordinator to confirm your **exact model and software version** for your examination session.


### Which IB Chemistry exam calculator is best?


A reliable scientific calculator is sufficient for most Chemistry calculations. It should handle brackets, scientific notation, powers, roots, logarithms, inverse logarithms, and exponentials efficiently.


A graphing display calculator, or **GDC** , is also suitable when approved and correctly configured. Its main benefit is familiarity if you already use it in Mathematics, since Chemistry rarely requires advanced graphing functions.


- **Best simple option:** a permitted scientific calculator used throughout the course.
- **Best shared Math and Chemistry option:** an approved TI-84 Plus, Casio fx-CG50, or equivalent school-supported GDC.
- **Best for an existing TI-Nspire user:** an approved model with the required Press-to-Test configuration.


Do not change calculators shortly before the examination merely to gain more functions. Speed comes from familiarity with brackets, menus, answer recall, and exponent entry.


### Calculators and tools you cannot use


Recent guidance identifies the **TI-89** , **TI Voyage 200** , older TI-Nspire CAS devices, and Casio ClassPad or fx-CG500 models as prohibited. Devices with unrestricted wireless access or unblocked prohibited functionality are also unsuitable.


You must not store notes, formulas, data, programs, or applications that replace examinable knowledge. Schools check devices and clear memory where required, but you should prepare yours beforehand under teacher supervision.


Phones, smartwatches, tablets, and online calculator applications cannot replace an approved physical calculator. A prohibited device in the examination room may create an academic integrity issue even if it is not used.


### Other required IB Chemistry tools


The[official specimen examinations](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/programmes/dp/pdfs/chemistry-hl-sl-specimen-papers-1a-2b-2-en.pdf) require a calculator and a **clean Chemistry data booklet** for Paper 1A, Paper 1B, and Paper 2. This differs from the course last assessed in 2024, when Paper 1 was completed without a calculator.


The booklet provides constants, equations, periodic data, spectra, and electrode potentials. An annotated revision copy cannot be taken into the examination. Learn its layout with the[RevisionDojo Chemistry data booklet reference](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-chemistry-new/data-booklet) , then follow your coordinator's instructions about the official copy.


Bring normal writing equipment and any stationery specified by your school, including a ruler for graphical work.


### How to use your calculator efficiently


### Enter complete expressions


Use brackets around full numerators and denominators. This reduces errors involving negative signs, division, and powers of ten.


### Master logarithms and exponentials


Acid-base problems commonly use pH = -log\[H+\]. Practise moving from concentration to pH and back without searching through calculator menus.


### Avoid premature rounding


Keep unrounded intermediate values by using answer recall. Round the final result according to the question, significant figures, or precision of the supplied data.


### Show chemical working


Write the equation, substitute values with units, and then calculate. A calculator display alone does not show your method and may not earn method marks if the final answer is incorrect.


### Check reasonableness


Estimate the expected sign and order of magnitude. Concentrations cannot be negative, while an exothermic enthalpy change normally has a negative sign.


Practise with the[IB Chemistry Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-chemistry-new/questionbank) using your real calculator and a clean booklet. The guide to[using the Chemistry data booklet](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-chemistry-how-to-use-data-booklet) also explains formula selection and unit conversion.


### Pre-exam calculator checklist


- Confirm the exact model with your coordinator.
- Install approved software before the examination.
- Learn the required exam mode with your teacher.
- Remove prohibited notes, programs, variables, and applications.
- Charge the device or install fresh batteries.
- Test logarithms, scientific notation, brackets, and answer recall.
- Complete timed papers with the same calculator and a clean booklet.


### Conclusion


The best **IB Chemistry exam calculator** is an approved, dependable device whose essential functions you can use confidently. Scientific calculators are normally sufficient, while permitted GDCs are practical when they are already familiar and correctly configured.


Verify permission through your coordinator and practise showing equations, substitutions, units, and sensible rounding.
